target_customer: Developers and small teams who run several AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent) in parallel
problem: Past two or three concurrent agent sessions the human becomes the bottleneck, answering small questions and unable to tell which sessions are progressing, stuck or building the wrong thing.
business_model: Free desktop app and CLI (Maxxwell) where users bring their own agent subscriptions or API keys; monetization not stated
product_category: Developer tools, multi-agent coding orchestration desktop app

founders.name: Michael Serrano
education: MIT, SB and MEng in Physics and Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page bio.

founders.name: Arthur De Los Santos
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page bio; no prior employers listed.

competitors.name: Maestro (RunMaestro)
competitors.what: Cross-platform desktop app to orchestrate a fleet of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode)

competitors.name: Agent Orchestrator
competitors.what: Apache-2.0 desktop workspace giving each agent session an isolated git worktree

competitors.name: Mozzie
competitors.what: Open-source local-first desktop tool for parallel AI coding agents

technical_complexity.rationale: Wrapping real terminal sessions of third party agents across macOS, Windows and Linux plus a supervising orchestrator agent is standard engineering with some hard parts around session state detection.

defensibility.rationale: Free product built on unmodified third party tools, with several open source orchestrators already available, so copying is easy and switching costs are low.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know; the agent vendors own the underlying tools and could ship native multi-session views.

market_need_then: Heavy use of parallel coding agents in 2026 created a supervision bottleneck, and many open source orchestrators appeared at the same time, showing the pain is widely felt.

branding.domain_note: Product site is maxxwell.dev, not the company name; no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, short imperative headlines such as 'Stop babysitting your agents.'

branding.brand_signature: The tagline 'The IDE for Tokenmaxxers' playing on internet maxxing slang

brand_strength.rationale: Company name Rindler and product name Maxxwell differ and neither is explained; no press about the brand was found, only directory listings.

outcome_analysis: Rindler is a two person MIT team in the Summer 2026 batch that, per the YC page, launched with a web-to-API product for agents but now sells Maxxwell, a free multi-agent coding desktop app. No outcome exists yet. The wedge is real but crowded with open source orchestrators and exposed to the agent vendors adding native supervision.
notes: The YC page launch post describes a different product (turn websites into APIs for agents) from the YC profile text (Maxxwell). Dealroom lists a $125k Seed and EveryDev lists $500000 raised; both are unverified aggregator figures, so no round is recorded. HQ varies (Boston vs San Francisco).
